Thought: Let me analyze each option for treating chemical burns:

A. Immediately remove the wetted clothing - This is generally recommended as chemicals on clothing can continue to cause damage to the skin.

B. Sprinkle flour on the wetted skin - This is not a recommended treatment for chemical burns. Flour could potentially trap chemicals against the skin or make the situation worse.

C. Sprinkle on neutralizing agents - This is not recommended for first aid. Attempting to neutralize chemicals can cause heat-generating reactions that may worsen the burn.

D. Wash the skin with plenty of water - This is the universally recommended first response to chemical burns. Dilution with water helps remove the chemical and minimize damage.

The standard first aid protocol for chemical burns is to flush the affected area with plenty of water. This dilutes and removes the chemical, preventing further damage. While removing contaminated clothing (option A) is also important, the primary and most critical step is to wash with water.
